# Grid header menu: trigger, floating surface and the wired value picker

## Context

Surface leaf of #19643 (graduated from [D#19646](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19646) at `eaae5352…`; pre-work review [6127438609](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19643#issuecomment-6127438609)): the header integration. It hosts the value-picker list (#19670) in a floating surface opened from the column header and wires it to the core leaf's shared contribution and counts (#19669). Blocked by both.

## The Problem

A header button today sorts on click (`src/grid/header/Button.mjs:274`), resizes at its right edge (`Resizable`, `directions: ['r']`, `src/grid/header/plugin/Resizable.mjs:28`, attached per button from `afterSetResizable`, `Button.mjs:178–192`), reorders by drag (`src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:304` ignores `.neo-resizable` for drag) and optionally shows an inline filter field (`Button.mjs:196–236`). There is no way to open a per-column surface, and nothing writes an owned picker contribution or shows contextual counts. The accepted contract (epic body, *Intended solution*): a per-column floating surface with context-menu, hover and focus activation, keyboard and touch paths, Escape and outside-pointer dismissal and focus return; the surface projects authoritative Store state and never resurrects cached selections; sort, resize and drag keep working.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.component.Base` owns the floating primitive: `align_` (`src/component/Base.mjs:79`) and `floating_` (`:135`), worker-side alignment, the `neo-floating` layer; a floating component that mounts moves focus into its first focusable item (`:137`).
- `Neo.form.field.Picker#createPicker` (`src/form/field/Picker.mjs:165–200`) is the established owner-local pattern: a floating `container.Base` on `document.body` aligned to the field's input wrapper (`edgeAlign`, `axisLock`, `matchSize`), `parentComponent` set to the owner, hidden until shown, `hiddenChange` observed.
- `Neo.menu.List` is the established interaction island: the app main view's outside-pointer listener kept symmetric with the root's mounted lifecycle (`src/menu/List.mjs:266–282`), `isInteractionPath` (`:504`) and `onAppMouseDown` (`:508–516`) dismiss on an outside pointer, `onKeyDownEscape` (`:808–817`) dismisses the root. Its full-cardinality rendering does not transfer (#19670).
- `contextmenu` is a routed DOM event (`src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:20`, `:39`); `onClick` already ignores `neo-resizable` paths (`Button.mjs:275`); the header SortZone ignores `.neo-resizable` for drag (`Toolbar.mjs:304`), so the trigger uses the same exclusion to stay out of sort and drag.
- `grid.Container` attaches plugins lazily behind a config (`afterSetCellEditing`, `src/grid/Container.mjs:372–410`): the config governs the plugin once created and a hand-declared plugin stays the app's own; `header.Button#afterSetResizable` is the per-button twin.
- The core seam proposed in #19669: `Filter.ownerRole` (`'header-picker'` from this surface), `getFilter(property, ownerRole)`, the `typedIncluded` operator, `Store.getFilterValues(property, excludeFilter)` → `{key, value, count}` buckets, `reapplyOnRecordChange`; the collection's `filter` event (`src/collection/Base.mjs:982`) is the re-projection trigger.
- Scale witness: `examples/grid/bigData` (`GridContainer.mjs:53–75`: `firstname`, `lastname` and `numberN` columns over the Turbo `MainStore`).

Pre-Flight (structural fast-path): authoring `src/grid/header/plugin/Menu.mjs` matches the sibling pattern of `src/grid/header/plugin/Resizable.mjs` (a per-button header plugin imported lazily from a `header.Button` config); sibling-file-lift applies; no novel directory choice. Map-maintenance: not needed.

## The Fix

- `Neo.grid.header.plugin.Menu` (new): attached per `header.Button` from a new button config (proposed `columnMenu_`, propagated like `resizable` from a column-level opt-in and a `grid.Container` default; names decided at intake). It renders a trigger node at the button's right edge, left of the resize handle, visible on hover and on `:focus-visible` of the button; it handles `contextmenu` on the button, the trigger click, and Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key on the focused button; all open the same surface.
- The surface: a floating `container.Base` on `document.body` (the `form.field.Picker` shape), aligned to the button node (`edgeAlign 't0-b0'`, `axisLock`), with items: a search `TextField` bound to the list's `searchValue`, the `list.ValuePicker` (#19670) and a Clear button. Outside-pointer and Escape dismissal through the `menu.List` island pattern (listener symmetric with mount); focus returns to the header button on dismissal; touch opens through the trigger.
- Wiring: on open, the plugin resolves its own contribution with `getFilter(dataField, 'header-picker')`, reads `store.getFilterValues(dataField, thatFilter)` into the host-owned options Store (label = a pure formatter of the typed value, or `String(value)`; never the cell renderer, which may depend on record, row or DOM context the picker does not have), and projects the contribution's value set into `selection`; the options Store is rebuilt as the union of the contribution's selected typed values and the returned buckets, absent keys at count 0, with Dates and explicit `undefined` preserved through the host's key-to-value mapping (a Model setter can turn `undefined` into `null`, so the mapping carries a discriminating control). On `selectionChange` it writes one `typedIncluded` filter with `ownerRole: 'header-picker'`, or removes it when the set empties; on the Store's `filter` event and on record changes it re-reads buckets and selection while open; Clear removes the contribution. The plugin observes the button's `dataField` and the Store reference: a retarget detaches the previous Store's borrowed observers synchronously, re-resolves the contribution on the new tuple and re-projects without writing (projection echoes suppressed); an external `store.filters` replacement re-projects from the `filter` event. Destroy disposes listeners, the options Store and the surface, and leaves the Store contribution in place (the lifetime table in the epic body).
- SCSS for the trigger and the surface under `resources/scss/src/grid/header/` (siblings `Button.scss`, `Toolbar.scss`); a Grids guide section.
- Evidence: a unit spec for the plugin's open, close, focus return and the contribution write and read (`test/playwright/unit/grid/`), whitebox e2e journeys on bigData through production input paths (`test/playwright/e2e/grid/`, sibling `BigDataNL.spec.mjs`), and the 100k witness.

## Design read (for the operator, before the PR)

The trigger is a small glyph at the header's right edge, just left of the resize handle, invisible until the header is hovered or keyboard-focused, so a plain header looks as it does today. A right-click anywhere on the header, a click on the trigger, Shift+F10 on the focused header, or a tap on the trigger opens the same surface under the header, left-aligned with it: a search field on top, the value list below (rows: checkbox, label, count), and a Clear link at the bottom while a selection exists. Checks apply immediately; the grid filters as you tick. Escape or a click outside closes the surface and focus returns to the header. Sorting by click, resizing by drag and reordering by drag behave exactly as before. On a store the picker cannot count honestly (remote, partial, tree, complex Turbo fields) the surface says so instead of showing numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: With the opt-in on, a header shows the trigger on hover and on focus; a right-click on the header, a trigger click, Shift+F10 on the focused header and a touch tap on the trigger each open the surface aligned under the header; off by default there is no trigger and no handler.
- [ ] AC2: Sort on click, resize by drag and column reorder by drag are unchanged with the plugin on (the e2e drives all three on bigData through production pointer paths after a surface was opened and closed).
- [ ] AC3: Escape and an outside pointer-down close the surface and return focus to the header button; a pointer-down inside the surface or on the trigger does not close it.
- [ ] AC4: Checking values writes exactly one filter with `ownerRole: 'header-picker'` and the column's `dataField`; an inline header filter and an application predicate on the same property survive in both creation orders; unchecking the last value or Clear removes that contribution and nothing else.
- [ ] AC5: Two grids on one Store: a selection in A shows checked in B's picker with equal counts; counts exclude only the picker's own contribution; options and counts update while the picker is open after an append and after a record edit, without reopening.
- [ ] AC6: Header destroy and recreate re-attaches to the existing contribution without duplicating it; a column `dataField` retarget and a source Store swap each detach the old borrowed observers immediately and attach to the new tuple's contribution; an external `store.filters = [...]` replacement that drops the contribution unchecks the open picker, and one that keeps an equal tuple under a different owner leaves it unchecked; projection never echoes a write; destroying the plugin disposes the surface, the options Store and all listeners and leaves the Store contribution in place.
- [ ] AC7: The 100k witness on `examples/grid/bigData` in its normal Turbo configuration with a `firstname` picker: sampled raw item keys and values are unchanged by open, search and recount; counts equal a reference pass over `allItems`; recount, option-list update, visible-row and input latency during scroll and resize are measured together in the same App Worker and recorded on the PR, with an id-like high-cardinality column included and the cap's refine row shown.
- [ ] AC8: On an unsupported population the surface renders the honest refusal for the returned reason code and writes no filter; each documented code has a fixture-store journey.
- [ ] AC9: A Grids guide section documents the opt-in, the surface, the selection semantics and the coverage boundary; unit and e2e specs run green in their tiers.
- [ ] AC10: The existing inline header filter fields (Grid and Table `header.Button#filterField`) project their value and operator from the shared `header-inline` contribution on header recreation and on source rebind, and never write on projection; the core's writer isolation (#19669) is consumed, not duplicated. Whether this ships inside this leaf or as its own one-PR leaf is decided at intake; the obligation is not deferred with the Table menu.

## Out of Scope

Counting, ownership and typed identity (#19669); the list's projection, search narrowing and cap (#19670); sort, hide, lock and width entries, a column chooser and a grid-level toolbar (deferred by the contract); case or regex search; an exclusion-set mode; the Table header menu surface (a follow-up once the grid surface lands); the Table inline field's projection obligation stays in AC10.

## Avoided Traps

- Rendering the surface inside the header button's vdom: it is a floating root on `document.body`, like every picker and submenu.
- A main-thread measurement for positioning: `align` is worker-side.
- Caching the selection in the plugin: the checked state is a projection of the Store contribution, re-read on the `filter` event.
- Retaining the header or the surface in the filter's callback scope: the owned predicate is a pure Store and filter-lifetime object.
- Putting the trigger inside the resize handle's hit area, or letting its click reach `onClick` (sort) or the SortZone (drag).
- Counting from the mounted row buffer.

## Intake — valid-as-written, with source-grounded implementation choices

Both blockers are closed: `#19669` is delivered, and `#19670` closed through [#19709](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19709) at `f94f1b5dd1`. The guarded transfer from Ada is verified; no overlapping header-surface PR appears in the current open queue. The related SortZone test PR [#19710](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19710) merged at `6cf28083b2`; its two-file test delta changes no production swap algorithm.

Prior epic review: [6127438609](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19643#issuecomment-6127438609), plus Ada's [6136740569](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19643#issuecomment-6136740569). Existing user scope remains the optional value-filter surface; no new consumer obligation or acceptance reduction.

**Prescription checked:** `src/grid/header/plugin/Resizable.mjs` establishes the per-button plugin home. `form/field/Picker#createPicker` and `menu/List` own the floating alignment and interaction-island precedent. `Base.observeConfig` already observes Container `store`; no new Store-change API is needed. Keep one `columnMenu` opt-in, false on the Grid and inherited by columns unless overridden. The source Store owns `header-picker` and `header-inline`; neither plugin owns cached selection truth.

The source clarifies four implementation obligations:
- Both Grid/Table header `dataField` configs are currently plain; make their rebinding observable. A locked Grid column must resolve its header through the existing cross-region `Container.getButton`, rather than the center-only lookup.
- AC10 remains in this coherent leaf. Use one shared UI projection plugin beside the existing `src/plugin` classes, with borrowed Store listeners and event-suppressed field value/operator projection; the existing writers retain their owner-role API. Table's rebind listener calls need independent object copies, as Grid already uses.
- The Grid header is a native button. Use the established sibling-button composition for an enabled menu trigger; no nested interactive button. Exclude the entire trigger path before sort and drag admission, preserving the resize exclusion. A comma `ignoreDragSelector` would be wrong: the current SortZone checks one class on the first path node.
- Recount supplies one `optionsStore.data` batch. Keep selected typed keys—including absent values at count zero—in a key-to-value map so Model normalization cannot turn explicit undefined into null. Permanent trigger visibility applies under `(hover: none)`.

Structural fast-path: `Menu.mjs` is a header plugin beside `Resizable.mjs`; the shared projection plugin is a component-owned extension beside `plugin/Responsive.mjs` and `plugin/PrefixField.mjs`. Existing directory roles cover both; no new subsystem/map home. `src/Neo.mjs`, `src/core/Base.mjs` and `src/state/Provider.mjs` idioms remain the foundation; the borrowed Store is the existing multi-consumer authority, with no parallel provider or predicate service.
